description:
From the fz-kdt.186 refutation (2026-09-03, accb5cfbe). types/mod.rs:2432
runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities removes a negated signature's ARITY
outright, where the list axis (runtime_type_predicate_list_shapes) removes a
shape only for an exact-empty / exact-non-empty negation. So the surface
`{any, any} & not({int, int})` -- non-empty, it holds {:ok, :ok} -- projects
to a RuntimeTypePredicate that admits nothing (`!p.overlaps(&p)`), and since
all three lowerings read one projection, an arm compiled for that surface
emits a test that always fails: a live arm that never fires (a value in the
surface falls through to later arms or the fail node). Reproducer:
    let carved = t.difference(t.tuple(&[any, any]), t.tuple(&[int, int]));
    assert!(!t.is_empty(&carved));
    let p = t.runtime_type_predicate(&carved);
    assert!(!p.overlaps(&p));       // admits NOTHING
Same family: a ListShapes axis whose only head is `none` (the fz-kdt.186
review's P2), and brand_of("Z") projecting to the all-none predicate
(requires_any widens only cofinite brand sets; no production caller today).
This was the root of the hole the 186 refuter closed in the seat (an
untested self-blind position could separate a pair); the seat is now robust
to it, the PROJECTION is not fixed. FIX: a same-arity negation must subtract
per POSITION into the shape (the way the list axis subtracts only exact
shapes), degrading to arity-only (over-approximate) when it cannot; never
to empty. Red-first: the reproducer as a unit pin, and a three-door fixture
with a clause over a carved tuple surface. Also correct the stale
finite_set.rs:112-114 sentence ("never to drop an arm or to justify a
seat" -- contained_in feeds test_inside, a drop conjunct since 143).
CONCORDANCE: fz-kdt.146 (the list-clause degrade rule -- the honest
precedent this axis should follow), fz-kdt.107/119 (the tuple axis's
origin), fz-kdt.186 (the seat made robust to it).
title: [BUG] runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities drops an arity for ANY same-arity negation: `{any, any} & not({int, int})` (non-empty) projects to the empty predicate, so a live arm compiles to a test that never fires
